editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally. It maps every permission-table row to the correct action ("Required by" becomes "Kailangan para sa", "Cancel a job" becomes "Kanselahin ang isang job", "Close job session" becomes "Isara ang job session") and keeps backend, job and session consistent throughout.

The meaning is faithful all the way through. The Paulice single-shot claim, the PNA mechanism (absorbing the inverses of learned noise channels into observables) and the SLC claim of reduced PEC variance are all rendered correctly, so nothing here would mislead a learner. Entry [10] reads as translationese: "Nagpapahintulot ito para sa" is a word-for-word calque of "allows for", and "mas mahigpit na i-bound" is awkward. Entry [6] also has the calque "para sa kung paano magsimula". The product-name plural is also inconsistent: [0]/[1] keep "Qiskit addons" but [4] uses "Mga Qiskit addon".

examples.source: This allows for more efficient, targeted applications of Probabilistic Error Cancellation (PEC) with reduced variance.
examples.translation: Nagpapahintulot ito para sa mas episyente, targeted na aplikasyon ng Probabilistic Error Cancellation (PEC) na may mas kaunting variance.
examples.suggested: Dahil dito, mas episyente at mas nakatutok ang paggamit ng Probabilistic Error Cancellation (PEC), at mas mababa ang variance.
examples.why: 'Nagpapahintulot ... para sa' calques English 'allows for'. A native writer would restructure the sentence.

examples.source: uses classical simulations to more tightly bound the sensitivity to errors throughout the circuit
examples.translation: ang classical simulations para mas mahigpit na i-bound ang sensitivity sa mga error sa buong circuit
examples.suggested: ang mga classical simulation para mas mahigpit na matantya ang hangganan ng sensitivity sa mga error sa buong circuit
examples.why: 'i-bound' is a bare English verb borrowing that reads stiffly. The meaning (tighter upper bound) is preserved but could be clearer.

examples.source: for how to get started today
examples.translation: para sa kung paano magsimula ngayon
examples.suggested: para malaman kung paano magsimula ngayon
examples.why: 'para sa kung paano' is a literal calque of 'for how to'.

editor_note: Faithful and natural; the hedges in [9] are kept ("Marahil ang pinakamahalaga", "maaaring mas mabilis"), "seamlessly integrate" is rendered as "tuluy-tuloy na isama", and "transpiler pass" and "release notes" stay in English, consistent with the rest of the file.

Both rewritten entries are faithful: [16] "Opsyonal na tukuyin ang isang instance na gagamitin" keeps the optional sense, and [21] "Kopyahin at i-save ang ibinalik na bearer token" and "sa pamamagitan ng pagsasama ng CRN at bearer token sa mga header ng kahilingan" keep every step and condition, with the code left as it was.

The three rewritten headings are accurate and read naturally in Tagalog: "Modelo ng directed execution (beta)" in [1] and [2], and "Primitive na Executor" in [26]. The body still says "directed execution model" and "Executor primitive" in English, but the headings' Tagalog word order is a defensible choice, not a defect.

None of the 9 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. They keep the precision-precedence logic, the twirling failure caveat in [36] ("mabibigo ang job kung ... mas maliit kaysa sa mga shots na kailangan") and the note in [20] that the options class need not be instantiated. There are two small slips. Entry [71] translates the link label as "Dokumentasyon ng `environment` API", but [81] and every other accordion keep "`execution` API documentation" in English, so the same label now appears two ways. In [25], "take precedence over" becomes "nangunguna sa" ("leads/comes first"), which is a weak fit for override semantics; "nananaig sa" says it more precisely.

examples.source: [`environment` API documentation](...)
examples.translation: [Dokumentasyon ng `environment` API](...)
examples.suggested: [`environment` API documentation](...)
examples.why: Every other API link label on the page, including the rewritten [81], stays as '`X` API documentation'. Only this one is translated, so the same label is rendered two ways in one file.

examples.source: They take precedence over any values specified as options
examples.translation: Ang mga ito ay nangunguna sa anumang mga halagang tinukoy bilang mga opsyon
examples.suggested: Ang mga ito ay nananaig sa anumang mga halagang itinakda bilang mga opsyon
examples.why: 'Nangunguna' means to lead or come first. For 'take precedence', meaning the value overrides the others, 'nananaig' is the clearer technical wording. The meaning still comes through, so this is minor.

editor_note: Entry 26 renders the heading "Dynamical Decoupling" as "Dynamical na Decoupling". That splits a fixed technique name with a Tagalog linker, as if "dynamical" were an ordinary adjective, and the result is neither natural Tagalog nor the recognized term. It also doesn't match entry 24, which keeps "dynamical decoupling" whole, or the sibling headings "TREX + ZNE" and "Twirling", which stay in English. The meaning is still clear and no learner would be misled, but the heading should read "Dynamical Decoupling".

examples.source: Dynamical Decoupling {#dynamical-decoupling}
examples.translation: Dynamical na Decoupling {#dynamical-decoupling}
examples.suggested: Dynamical Decoupling {#dynamical-decoupling}
examples.why: This is the name of an error-suppression technique, and the field keeps it as one English term. Putting "na" between the two words turns it into a hybrid calque. It also doesn't match entry 24 ("dynamical decoupling"), which uses the same term on this page, or the sibling headings Twirling and TREX + ZNE, which are left in English.

editor_note: The rewritten heading in entry 2 renders "Fair-share scheduler" as "Scheduler na Fair-share". The meaning is intact, so it won't mislead a learner. It does break the page's own convention: the title in entry 1 and every body occurrence (entries 0, 3, 7, 10, 14) keep "fair-share scheduler" as a fixed compound. The reordered linker form with a capitalized "Fair-share" reads stiff next to them. A native editor would make it match entry 1 exactly.

examples.source: Fair-share scheduler {#fair-share-scheduler}
examples.translation: Scheduler na Fair-share {#fair-share-scheduler}
examples.suggested: Fair-share scheduler {#fair-share-scheduler}
examples.why: Inconsistent with the page title (entry 1, 'Fair-share scheduler') and the body, which keep 'fair-share scheduler' as a fixed term. The inverted 'Scheduler na Fair-share' with a capitalized modifier reads awkwardly. This is a minor inconsistency and doesn't change the meaning.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The inputs table, the batches/6073 sizing explanation, the rule that estimator_options replaces the defaults instead of merging, and the reconnect steps all match the English, and I found no drift or hallucination. What's left is style. Some phrasing is redundant: "Mas alamin pa nang mas malalim" in [78] and "tig-1000 circuit bawat isa" in [59]. Some wording is calqued: "Umuunlad hanggang T" for "evolves to" in [39] and "bibilangin laban sa mga ito" in [60]. In [64], the singular "itong" refers to two settings (DD and TREX), so it should be "ang mga ito". "pinaka-hindi-busy" for "least busy" is awkward but still clear.

examples.source: Go deeper on the AQC compression stage with the ... documentation.
examples.translation: Mas alamin pa nang mas malalim ang AQC compression stage gamit ang dokumentasyon ng ...
examples.suggested: Palalimin ang pag-unawa sa AQC compression stage gamit ang dokumentasyon ng ...
examples.why: 'Mas' appears twice, which makes the sentence redundant.

examples.source: so dynamical decoupling and TREX are restated in the following cell to keep them switched on.
examples.translation: ...para mapanatili itong naka-on.
examples.suggested: ...para manatiling naka-on ang mga ito.
examples.why: 'itong' is singular, but it refers to two settings: DD and TREX.

examples.source: Evolves to `T = t_steps * dt`
examples.translation: Umuunlad hanggang `T = t_steps * dt`
examples.suggested: Ine-evolve ang state hanggang `T = t_steps * dt`
examples.why: 'Umuunlad' means to progress or develop. It is not the usual rendering of time evolution in physics.

examples.source: submits 11 PUBs of 1000 circuits each
examples.translation: nagsu-submit ng 11 PUB na tig-1000 circuit bawat isa
examples.suggested: nagsu-submit ng 11 PUB na tig-1000 circuit
examples.why: 'tig-' already means 'each', so 'bawat isa' repeats it.

editor_note: Both rewritten accordion titles are faithful and natural in a casual register: "I-click upang palawakin para sa karagdagang detalye tungkol sa mga kinakailangang opsyon:" [24] and "...tungkol sa pag-configure ng mga opsyon ng SQD:" [35].

The meaning is faithful throughout: the job-status list, the capacity pre-check in run(), the note on runtime_jobs() and the API-key caveats all match the English. There are a few spots a native editor would still fix. In [34], "raises an error" is calqued literally as "magpapataas ... ng error", which says the error gets "increased". In [25], "Alamin pa ang higit pa" is redundant, and in [63], "Mag-page-through" is an awkward hybrid. "Credentials" is also rendered two ways: "kredensyal" in [20] and "credential" in [23].

examples.source: `run()` raises an error right away
examples.translation: agad na magpapataas ang `run()` ng error
examples.suggested: agad na maglalabas ng error ang `run()`
examples.why: 'Magpataas' means to raise in the sense of increasing or lifting, so it is a literal calque of the programming idiom. 'Maglabas ng error' is the natural Tagalog phrase.

examples.source: Learn more in the [Managing user API keys] topic.
examples.translation: Alamin pa ang higit pa sa [Managing user API keys] topic.
examples.suggested: Alamin pa sa [Managing user API keys] topic.
examples.why: 'Alamin pa ang higit pa' says 'more' twice. Entry [27] already uses the cleaner 'Alamin pa sa'.

examples.source: you can load your credentials
examples.translation: maaari mong i-load ang iyong mga credential
examples.suggested: maaari mong i-load ang iyong mga kredensyal
examples.why: Entry [20] uses 'kredensyal', so the same term appears two ways on one page.

examples.source: Page through results with `limit` and `offset`
examples.translation: Mag-page-through ng mga resulta gamit ang `limit` at `offset`
examples.suggested: Hatiin sa mga pahina ang mga resulta gamit ang `limit` at `offset`
examples.why: 'Mag-page-through' is an awkward hybrid a Tagalog technical writer would not use.

editor_note: Entry 50's heading "Mode na Strict" keeps the meaning of "Strict mode" and uses the normal Tagalog noun-linker-modifier order, so it is a defensible choice. It also points clearly to the `strict=True` "letter-of-the-spec" mode described in entry 51.

Entry 9 matches the English. "kung pinagana mo ang Pauli-twirling" keeps the condition, and "ang kabuuang bilang ng shots ay nakabatay sa mga value ng `num_randomizations` at `shots_per_randomization`" keeps the dependency. "shots" is used the same way as elsewhere in the file.

I only judged the five rewritten entries (12, 13, 57, 71, 86), and none of them would mislead a learner. Entry 12 keeps the "no simulator yet" caveat and the local-sampling workaround. Entry 57 correctly says Executor needs annotated boxes and a samplex. Entry 71 renders "where settings live" as "kung saan itinatakda ang mga setting", which matches entry 73. The one slip is in entry 13: "considerably more involved" becomes just "mas kumplikado", so the intensifier that signals how much harder Estimator migration is gets lost.

examples.source: Migrating from Estimator to Executor is considerably more involved than migrating from Sampler
examples.translation: Ang paglipat mula sa Estimator patungo sa Executor ay mas kumplikado kaysa sa paglipat mula sa Sampler
examples.suggested: Ang paglipat mula sa Estimator patungo sa Executor ay mas kumplikado nang malaki kaysa sa paglipat mula sa Sampler
examples.why: The qualifier 'considerably' is dropped, so the claim is weaker than in the English. This is a dropped qualifier (MINOR), not a reversal of meaning.

editor_note: The rewritten heading in entry 8, "Mga OVHcloud AI notebook", is faithful, uses the natural Tagalog "Mga" plural with the English noun left uninflected, and matches the wording in the entry 10 admonition ("ang mga OVHcloud AI notebook").

The body of entry 9 is faithful. "Simula 16 Marso 2026" keeps the date, "mag-opt in para sa karagdagang 180 minuto sa loob ng susunod na 12 buwan" keeps the 180 minutes and the 12-month window, and the eligibility condition ("aktibong user ng Open Plan") is kept too. The one change I'd make is the title. "Limitadong Promosyon" drops "time", so it reads as a limited promotion rather than a limited-time one. The title is the only place that says the opt-in offer itself is temporary, so "Promosyon sa Limitadong Panahon" would keep that caveat.

examples.source: title="Limited time promotion"
examples.translation: title="Limitadong Promosyon"
examples.suggested: title="Promosyon sa Limitadong Panahon"
examples.why: Dropping 'time' changes 'limited-time offer' to just 'limited promotion', which could mean limited in quantity or scope. The title is the only place that says the offer expires. This is a small weakening, not misleading, so it is minor.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries would mislead a learner, and entry 11, "Environment ng pag-compile", is fine. Entries 1 and 3 translate the product name as "Interface ng pamamahala ng quantum resource (QRMI)". Entries 0 and 4 keep the English name "Quantum Resource Management Interface", so the page title and heading no longer match the body text. Entry 25, "Environment ng Runtime", capitalizes "Runtime", which makes a generic phrase look like the Qiskit Runtime product; lowercase "runtime" matches the English.

examples.source: Quantum resource management interface (QRMI)
examples.translation: Interface ng pamamahala ng quantum resource (QRMI)
examples.suggested: Quantum resource management interface (QRMI)
examples.why: This is the product's proper name, and entries 0 and 4 keep it in English. Translating it only in the title and heading makes the page name the product two different ways. Entry 1 has the same problem.

examples.source: Runtime environment
examples.translation: Environment ng Runtime
examples.suggested: Environment ng runtime
examples.why: "Runtime" here is generic: the libraries needed when the program runs. The capital R makes it look like the Qiskit Runtime product, and it doesn't match the lowercase "pag-compile" in entry 11.

editor_note: Entries 18 and 25 are faithful. Entry 25 keeps the caveat that the options class "does not need to be instantiated if you are setting options after initializing": "Hindi na kailangang i-instantiate ... kung nagtatakda ka ng mga opsyon pagkatapos ng pagsisimula ng primitive". It also uses "pagsisimula" for initialization, which matches entries 15 and 23. The only issue is in the heading at entry 16: it renders "class" as "Klase na `options`", but the rest of the page keeps "class" in English. Entry 17 right below it says "`options` class", entry 18 says "tungkol sa class", and entries 6, 13 and 25 say "options class". The heading should use the same form. The linker "na" is also slightly awkward here.

examples.source: `options` class {#options-class}
examples.translation: Klase na `options` {#options-class}
examples.suggested: `options` class {#options-class}
examples.why: The rest of the page keeps 'class' in English: entry 17 has '`options` class', entry 18 has 'class', and entries 6, 13 and 25 have 'options class'. The heading alone switches to 'Klase', and 'Klase na' is a stiff linker choice. This does not mislead, but the heading should match the body text below it.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning, so neither would mislead a learner. Entry 6 has a typo: "sa pamamagian ng paggamit" should read "sa pamamagitan ng paggamit". Entry 30 follows English word order in "maglagay ng mga hangganan ng timestamp na itaas at ibaba sa kung kailan partikular na mga shot ay naisakatuparan", which reads stiffly and should be recast in natural Tagalog order. Term choices (trabaho for job, bagay for object, pamamaraan for method) match the rest of the file.

examples.source: by using a data structure known as a Primitive Unified Bloc (PUB)
examples.translation: sa pamamagian ng paggamit ng isang istraktura ng data
examples.suggested: sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng isang istraktura ng data
examples.why: Typo: 'pamamagian' is not a word. The intended word is 'pamamagitan'.

examples.source: This timing information can be used to place upper and lower timestamp bounds on when particular shots were executed on the QPU.
examples.translation: Ang impormasyong ito sa timing ay maaaring gamitin upang maglagay ng mga hangganan ng timestamp na itaas at ibaba sa kung kailan partikular na mga shot ay naisakatuparan sa QPU.
examples.suggested: Magagamit ang impormasyong ito sa timing para tukuyin ang pinakamaaga at pinakahuling timestamp kung kailan naisakatuparan sa QPU ang mga partikular na shot.
examples.why: It copies English word order ('hangganan ... na itaas at ibaba sa kung kailan'). The meaning is intact, but it reads like machine translation.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The get_runtime_service admonition ([31]-[32]) and the upload/tar explanation ([40]) are faithful. A native editor would still fix three spots. In [6], "Ang Qiskit Serverless ay nagpapabuti" uses an actor-focus verb with no object, so it reads as "Serverless is improving [something]" instead of "is being upgraded". [27] stacks "Limitado pa lang ... lamang" awkwardly and ends on the calqued "bilang string sa halip". [40] switches tense in "ini-upload at nilinis pagkatapos".

examples.source: Qiskit Serverless is getting an upgrade, and its features are changing fast.
examples.translation: Ang Qiskit Serverless ay nagpapabuti, at mabilis nagbabago ang mga feature nito.
examples.suggested: Ina-upgrade ang Qiskit Serverless, at mabilis na nagbabago ang mga feature nito.
examples.why: The actor-focus 'nagpapabuti' with no object says Serverless is improving something, not that it is being upgraded. The adverb linker 'na' is also missing after 'mabilis'.

examples.source: Serverless is currently limited to only accept serializable inputs and outputs. ... so use `backend_name` as a string instead.
examples.translation: Limitado pa lang ang Serverless na tumatanggap lamang ng serializable na mga input at output. ... kaya gamitin ang `backend_name` bilang string sa halip.
examples.suggested: Sa ngayon, serializable na input at output lang ang tinatanggap ng Serverless. ... kaya sa halip, gamitin ang `backend_name` bilang string.
examples.why: 'Limitado ... lamang' is redundant and calqued, and ending the sentence on 'sa halip' copies English word order.

examples.source: into a `tar`, which is uploaded and then cleaned up.
examples.translation: sa isang `tar`, na ini-upload at nilinis pagkatapos.
examples.suggested: sa isang `tar`, na ina-upload at pagkatapos ay nililinis.
examples.why: The tense switches from imperfective 'ini-upload' to perfective 'nilinis' for what is a routine process. It should use one consistent aspect.

editor_note: Entry 15 translates "Error detection" as "Pagtukoy ng Error", which is faithful and natural and matches "Maaaring matukoy ang error" in entry 19, so the heading reads as part of the same text.

Both rewritten entries are faithful and natural: entry 1 reads "Pagsusulit | Pangkalahatang Pagbubuo ng Quantum Information", and entry 12's Credly notice keeps every clause, including "awtorisado ng IBM at nakabase sa Estados Unidos", the three-item data list, sharing "sa buong mundo" and the "mga gawi ng IBM sa privacy" caveat, with no drift.

None of the six rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entries 60, 63 and 110 are faithful, and 80 is faithful too, just a bit stiff. In entry 79, "kinakailangang hatiin ng $n$ ang $m N$" says only that n divides mN in the everyday sense and loses the math meaning "divides evenly". Entry 80's statement that mN/n "maaaring hindi integer" makes the intended meaning recoverable. Entry 99 drops the logical connective "therefore" ("Mayroon na tayong…" instead of "Kaya mayroon na tayong…"), which weakens the link to the derivation before it.

examples.source: it must be that $n$ divides $m N$
examples.translation: kinakailangang hatiin ng $n$ ang $m N$
examples.suggested: kinakailangang mahati nang eksakto ng $n$ ang $m N$ (ibig sabihin, multiple ng $n$ ang $mN$)
examples.why: "Hatiin" just means "divide". The English means exact divisibility, and that is the whole point of the condition. It is only recoverable because entry 80 mentions integers.

examples.source: We therefore have a correct representation for the mapping $\Phi$
examples.translation: Mayroon na tayong tamang representasyon para sa mapping na $\Phi$
examples.suggested: Kaya mayroon na tayong tamang representasyon para sa mapping na $\Phi$
examples.why: The translation drops "therefore", so the conclusion no longer points back to the computation before it.

examples.source: by choosing $A_k = 0$ for however many additional values of $k$ that we wish
examples.translation: sa pamamagitan ng pagpili ng $A_k = 0$ para sa kung gaano karaming karagdagang halaga ng $k$ ang nais natin
examples.suggested: sa pamamagitan ng pagtatakda ng $A_k = 0$ para sa kahit ilang karagdagang halaga ng $k$ na gusto natin
examples.why: "Para sa kung gaano karaming" copies the English word order. "Kahit ilang" is how a Tagalog speaker would naturally say it.

editor_note: The four rewritten headings (26, 74, 134, 137) keep the meaning: "Ganap na Dephasing/Depolarizing Channel" correctly renders "Completely ... channel", and nothing here would mislead a learner. They do break consistency with the rest of the page. Sibling headings keep the English term ([45] "Completely dephasing channel (alternatibo)", [87] "Completely depolarizing channel"), and every body entry says "completely dephasing/depolarizing channel" ([29], [46], [75], [135], [138]). So the same channel now has a Tagalog-prefixed name in some headings and an English one everywhere else. The new headings also use Title Case ("Dephasing Channel"), while the other headings on the page use sentence case ("Mga unitary channel", "qubit reset channel"). Pick one form of the name for the headings and use it throughout.

examples.source: Completely dephasing channel {#completely-dephasing-channel}
examples.translation: Ganap na Dephasing Channel {#completely-dephasing-channel}
examples.suggested: Completely dephasing channel {#completely-dephasing-channel} (matching [45] and the body text), or else apply 'Ganap na dephasing channel' to [45] too
examples.why: The same channel name is split between the Tagalog-prefixed heading here and the English term in [45] and throughout the body ([29], [46], [75]). A learner can still recognize it, but the split looks unintended.

examples.source: Completely depolarizing channel {#completely-depolarizing-channel-1}
examples.translation: Ganap na Depolarizing Channel {#completely-depolarizing-channel-1}
examples.suggested: Completely depolarizing channel {#completely-depolarizing-channel-1}
examples.why: The earlier heading for the same channel ([87]) is 'Completely depolarizing channel', and [138] directly below uses the English term. This heading is also in Title Case, while the page's other headings use sentence case.

editor_note: Entry 14 (the video title) keeps the English meaning: it lists the same three applications (carbon capture, chemical structure for fertilizers, and new materials for higher-capacity batteries) and adds or drops nothing. One wording problem: "mga novel na materyales" keeps the English adjective "novel" with the Tagalog linker "na", which reads as a stiff calque. A native technical writer would write "mga bagong materyales" (new materials). It does not mislead a learner.

examples.source: the design of novel materials like those used to design higher capacity batteries
examples.translation: ang disenyo ng mga novel na materyales tulad ng mga ginagamit sa pagdisenyo ng mga baterya na may mas mataas na kapasidad
examples.suggested: ang disenyo ng mga bagong materyales tulad ng mga ginagamit sa pagdisenyo ng mga bateryang may mas mataas na kapasidad
examples.why: 'novel na materyales' keeps the English adjective 'novel' with a Tagalog linker, which is a calque. 'bagong materyales' is the natural wording and means the same thing. The sentence is still correct and would not mislead.

editor_note: Entry 7 says the same thing as the English. "Ipinapaliwanag ni Victoria Lipinska ang paggamit ng mga classical optimizer sa VQE" and "ang tinatawag na barren plateaus" keep both the claim and the "so-called" hedge, and "noise" is fine because entry 6 already glosses it as "ingay (noise)".

The rewritten title [1] "QAOA sa Sukat ng Utility" translates "utility-scale" word for word. Everywhere else on the page the term stays in English as a modifier: "utility-scale QAOA" in [3], and "utility-scale na halimbawa" and "utility-scale na problema" in [0], [6] and [7]. The title therefore doesn't match the body text. "Sukat ng Utility" also reads awkwardly, like "the measure of utility," though a learner would not be misled. Use the same rendering as the body, for example "Utility-scale na QAOA".

examples.source: Utility-scale QAOA
examples.translation: QAOA sa Sukat ng Utility
examples.suggested: Utility-scale na QAOA
examples.why: The title translates 'utility-scale' literally, but the rest of the file keeps it in English ([0], [3], [6], [7]). The heading and body end up with two different terms for one concept, and 'Sukat ng Utility' is stiff and ambiguous in Tagalog.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries match the English: entry 5 renders the survey request faithfully ("maikling survey", "pahusayin ang aming content offering at user experience"), and entry 12 keeps every part of the Credly notice, including the list of shared data ("pangalan, email address, at badge na natanggap"), the "Maaaring ibahagi" caveat and "sa buong mundo".

Entry 29 translates "implicitly adopting" as "tahasan nating ginagamit". "Tahasan" means explicitly or openly, so the sentence now says the opposite of the English. The note exists to explain that the ket/column-vector convention is only implicit: NumPy 1D arrays do not enforce it and the transpose does nothing. Saying the convention is explicit contradicts the rest of the paragraph and would mislead a learner. A smaller issue is that "walang epekto sa numero" and "parehong resulta sa numero" are stiff calques of "no numerical effect" and "same numerical result".

examples.source: we are implicitly adopting the common convention that the state vectors `x1` and `x2` correspond to kets (column vectors)
examples.translation: tahasan nating ginagamit ang karaniwang convention na ang mga state vector na `x1` at `x2` ay katumbas ng mga ket (column vector)
examples.suggested: hindi-tahasan (implicitly) nating ginagamit ang karaniwang convention na ang mga state vector na `x1` at `x2` ay katumbas ng mga ket (column vector)
examples.why: 'Tahasan' means explicitly, the opposite of 'implicitly'. The paragraph's point is that NumPy does not enforce the convention, so calling it explicit contradicts what follows.

examples.source: the transpose operation has no numerical effect ... would produce the same numerical result
examples.translation: ang transpose operation ay walang epekto sa numero ... ay magbibigay ng parehong resulta sa numero
examples.suggested: hindi nagbabago ang numerical na resulta dahil sa transpose operation ... ay magbibigay ng parehong numerical na resulta
examples.why: 'Sa numero' is a stiff calque of 'numerical'. It reads as 'on the number' rather than 'on the computed values'.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries (6, 24, 57) would mislead a learner. Entry 6 is complete in the paired file, keeps all three categories and ends with "reward at parusa". Entry 24 keeps the bolded __hindi__ and the caveat that high-dimensional quantum states are not enough to beat classical methods. The problems are wording only. Entry 6 renders "grouped" as "ihiwalay" (separated) where "ipangkat" is the natural word. Entry 24 uses the calque "itakda ang entablado" and the stiff "pagpapabuti kaysa sa". The heading in entry 57, "Perceptron ng Quantum", is a genitive calque that reads as "perceptron of quantum". It also clashes with the sibling heading "Quantum neural network" (entry 59), which keeps "quantum" as a modifier, so it should be "Quantum perceptron".

examples.source: Quantum perceptron {#quantum-perceptron}
examples.translation: Perceptron ng Quantum {#quantum-perceptron}
examples.suggested: Quantum perceptron {#quantum-perceptron}
examples.why: The genitive 'ng Quantum' reads as 'perceptron of quantum' and has a stray capital. It is also inconsistent with the sibling heading 'Quantum neural network' (entry 59) and with 'quantum na katapat ng perceptron' in entry 58.

examples.source: machine learning algorithms can be grouped into three main categories
examples.translation: ang mga machine learning algorithm ay maaaring ihiwalay sa tatlong pangunahing kategorya
examples.suggested: ang mga machine learning algorithm ay maaaring ipangkat sa tatlong pangunahing kategorya
examples.why: 'ihiwalay' means 'to separate' or 'isolate'. 'ipangkat' (to group) matches 'grouped' and reads more naturally.

examples.source: and thus set the stage for what a quantum kernel is ... are not sufficient for improvement over classical methods
examples.translation: at sa gayon ay itakda ang entablado para sa kung ano ang quantum kernel ... ay hindi sapat para sa pagpapabuti kaysa sa mga klasikal na paraan
examples.suggested: at sa gayon ay ihanda ang daan para maunawaan kung ano ang quantum kernel ... ay hindi sapat para malampasan ang mga klasikal na paraan
examples.why: 'itakda ang entablado' is a literal calque of the idiom 'set the stage', and 'pagpapabuti kaysa sa' is a stiff comparative. The meaning is faithful, so this is a wording fix only.

editor_note: None of the 12 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The long prose entries (39 on amplitude normalization, 181 on the PFM/Ising analogy and "linear" entanglement) are faithful and keep their caveats. The rewritten section headings no longer match the body, which still uses the English-order terms: headings say "Pag-encode ng Amplitude", "Pag-encode ng Angle" and "Feature Map ng $Z$", while the body says "amplitude encoding", "angle encoding" and "$Z$ feature map". "Dense na Pag-encode ng Angle" and "Pag-encode ng Basis" are stiff calques, and "ng Basis" reads as "encoding the basis" when the method actually encodes data into basis states. There are also two small slips: entry 8 renders "we will mostly refer to" as "mag-iisip tayo tungkol sa" ("we will think about"), and entry 84 ends on a bare English "anyway".

examples.source: Basis encoding {#basis-encoding}
examples.translation: Pag-encode ng Basis {#basis-encoding}
examples.suggested: Basis encoding {#basis-encoding}
examples.why: The body uses "basis encoding" throughout (entries 20, 21, 33), so the heading differs from the term the learner then reads. "Pag-encode ng Basis" also suggests encoding the basis itself rather than encoding data into basis states. The same heading/body split affects entries 36, 70, 90, 147, 159 and 174.

examples.source: Dense angle encoding {#dense-angle-encoding}
examples.translation: Dense na Pag-encode ng Angle {#dense-angle-encoding}
examples.suggested: Dense angle encoding {#dense-angle-encoding}
examples.why: This is a stiff hybrid calque, and entry 109 immediately calls the method "dense angle encoding (DAE)".

examples.source: But we will mostly refer to the loading of a single vector from our dataset at a time
examples.translation: Ngunit kadalasan ay mag-iisip tayo tungkol sa pag-load ng isang vector mula sa ating dataset sa isang pagkakataon
examples.suggested: Ngunit kadalasan ay tatalakayin natin ang pag-load ng isang vector mula sa ating dataset sa isang pagkakataon
examples.why: "mag-iisip tayo tungkol sa" means "we will think about", not "refer to / discuss". It is a small shift in meaning and does not mislead.

examples.source: especially since data should be rescaled to the $(0,2\pi]$ interval, anyway.
examples.translation: lalo na dahil dapat i-rescale ang data sa $(0,2\pi]$ interval anyway.
examples.suggested: lalo na dahil dapat naman talagang i-rescale ang data sa $(0,2\pi]$ interval.
examples.why: A bare English "anyway" at the end of the sentence reads as unedited Taglish. "naman talaga" gives the same nuance in Tagalog.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The DD walkthrough, the XX/XY4 comparison and the GHZ accidental-protection argument ([137]-[152]) all keep their meaning. One sentence comes close: the definition of coherent accumulation in [81] turns "tend to drive errors in the same direction" into the garbled "palaging tumatawid sa parehong direksyon ng error", which reads as "always crosses" and states the hedge as a certainty. Some comparisons also lose their emphasis: "much lower" in [46] and "much larger" in [106] both become plain "mas mababa"/"mas malaki", and "tend to" is dropped in [83]. The register also shifts from casual "para/pero" to more formal "upang/ngunit/gayunpaman" from about [141] on, and there are a few calques ("Naglingkod ang halimbawang ito para sa layunin nito", "Ang kapaki-pakinabang na ito", "bibisualisahin").

examples.source: Coherent accumulation of errors means that noise or imperfect implementations all tend to drive errors in the same direction across multiple layers and gates.
examples.translation: ...ang noise o imperpektong implementasyon ay palaging tumatawid sa parehong direksyon ng error sa maraming layers at gates.
examples.suggested: ...ang noise o imperpektong implementasyon ay may tendensiyang itulak ang mga error sa iisang direksyon sa maraming layers at gates.
examples.why: 'tend to drive' becomes 'palaging tumatawid' ('always crosses'). That states the hedge as a certainty and uses the wrong verb, which blurs the key definition.

examples.source: Error rates associated with two-qubit gates are much larger than those associated with single-qubit gates.
examples.translation: Ang error rates na kaugnay sa two-qubit gates ay mas malaki kaysa sa mga kaugnay sa single-qubit gates.
examples.suggested: ...ay mas malaki nang husto kaysa sa mga kaugnay sa single-qubit gates.
examples.why: Dropping 'much' weakens the reason twirling is only applied around two-qubit gates. The same slip appears in [46] ('much lower' becomes 'mas mababa').

examples.source: The usefulness of this will become more apparent in the context of error-mitigation techniques
examples.translation: Ang kapaki-pakinabang na ito ay magiging mas malinaw sa konteksto ng mga teknik sa error-mitigation
examples.suggested: Magiging mas malinaw ang pagiging kapaki-pakinabang nito sa konteksto ng mga teknik sa error-mitigation
examples.why: 'Ang kapaki-pakinabang na ito' uses an adjective as if it were a noun. It is ungrammatical and stiff.

examples.source: This example served its purpose, but let's move onto something more useful
examples.translation: Naglingkod ang halimbawang ito para sa layunin nito, pero lumipat tayo sa mas kapaki-pakinabang na bagay
examples.suggested: Nagawa na ng halimbawang ito ang layunin nito, pero lumipat na tayo sa mas kapaki-pakinabang
examples.why: 'Naglingkod ... para sa layunin nito' is a word-for-word calque of 'served its purpose'.

examples.source: ...often used to cancel coherent ZZ error terms in two-qubit gates, even without twirling. But with twirling, we can reduce...
examples.translation: ...madalas gamitin upang kanselahin ang coherent ZZ error term sa two-qubit gates, kahit walang twirling. Ngunit sa twirling, mababawasan...
examples.suggested: ...madalas gamitin para kanselahin ... Pero sa twirling, mababawasan...
examples.why: The last third of the file switches to formal 'upang/ngunit/gayunpaman', which breaks the casual 'para/pero' register used earlier in the file.

editor_note: None of the 23 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The meaning holds in the hard spots too: the amplitude-damping shape in [205] (XY shrinks less than Z), the p→1 dephasing subtlety and the 50-50 minimum in [227], and the light-cone argument in [292]. What remains is small wording that a native editor would still fix. Bloch-sphere "pole" is rendered "poste" (post/pillar) in [205] and [218] where "polo" is meant. [240] "umiikot sa isang qubit" reads as "revolves around" rather than "rotates". [227] has the ungrammatical "dapat magulo ang ating phase" and a misused "basta't" ("as long as"). [211] has the typo "paggiging", and [279] uses the awkward "nagkakamaling state" for "erroneous state".

examples.source: shifted upward toward the $|0\rangle$ pole
examples.translation: lumipat pataas patungo sa poste ng $|0\rangle$
examples.suggested: lumipat pataas patungo sa polo ng $|0\rangle$
examples.why: 'poste' means a post or pillar; the pole of a sphere is 'polo'. Same issue in [218]: 'nahuhulog sa isang poste'.

examples.source: A single-qubit gate rotates an isolated qubit.
examples.translation: Ang isang single-qubit gate ay umiikot sa isang nakahiwalay na qubit.
examples.suggested: Ang isang single-qubit gate ay nagpapaikot sa isang nakahiwalay na qubit.
examples.why: 'umiikot sa' means 'revolves around'. The gate acts on the qubit, so the causative form is needed.

examples.source: a high probability of a dephasing error should mess up our phase, right? ... the phase has simply flipped.
examples.translation: ay dapat magulo ang ating phase, tama ba? ... basta't nabaligtad lamang ang phase.
examples.suggested: ay dapat gumulo sa ating phase, tama ba? ... nabaligtad lang talaga ang phase.
examples.why: 'dapat magulo ang ating phase' is ungrammatical here, and 'basta't' means 'as long as', not 'simply'.

examples.source: or as the system becoming more classical
examples.translation: o bilang paggiging mas klasiko ng sistema
examples.suggested: o bilang pagiging mas klasiko ng sistema
examples.why: Spelling error: the correct word is 'pagiging'.

examples.source: what error combination applied after the CNOT would yield the erroneous state, and in particular
examples.translation: ang magbubunga ng nagkakamaling state, at higit sa lahat
examples.suggested: ang magbubunga ng state na may error, at partikular na
examples.why: 'nagkakamaling' means 'making a mistake', which is odd for a state. 'higit sa lahat' ('above all') also overstates 'in particular'.

editor_note: The rewritten entry [2] heading, "Klasikal na simulasyon", is accurate and won't mislead anyone. The problem is consistency: the entries right around it keep the English term. [0] and [3] say "tungkol sa classical simulation", and the lesson title in [1] is "Aralin 08 Classical simulation". So the page title and its own H1 now use two different forms. To match the rest of the page, change the heading to "Classical simulation", or else translate the term the same way everywhere.

examples.source: Classical simulation {#classical-simulation}
examples.translation: Klasikal na simulasyon {#classical-simulation}
examples.suggested: Classical simulation {#classical-simulation}
examples.why: Entries [0], [1] and [3] keep 'classical simulation' in English, including the lesson title just before this heading. Translating it only here splits the term within the file. It's still recognizable, so this is a minor issue.

editor_note: Entry 48 is faithful and natural: "mga opsyon ng pagpapagaan ng error" matches the heading in [46], and the link label "I-configure ang pagpapagaan ng error" matches the one in [42]. "Panimula sa mga opsyon" reads naturally and the link targets are unchanged.

Entry 3, "Utility-scale na eksperimento I", is faithful and matches the page's own "utility-scale na eksperimento" in [68]. Entry 64 turns the heading "5.3 Post-process" into "Pagpoproseso Pagkatapos". That breaks the page's convention: the parallel heading [55] "4.4 Hakbang 4: Post-process" and the Qiskit-pattern step name in [48]/[49] keep "Post-process" as the named step. The capitalized word-by-word calque also reads stiffly. It does not mislead a learner, but the heading should read "5.3 Post-process" (or "Hakbang 4: Post-process") so it lines up with 4.4 and the four-step workflow.

examples.source: 5.3 Post-process {#53-post-process}
examples.translation: 5.3 Pagpoproseso Pagkatapos {#53-post-process}
examples.suggested: 5.3 Post-process {#53-post-process}
examples.why: The parallel section [55] and the Qiskit pattern steps in [48]/[49] keep 'Post-process' as the step name. Translating it only here breaks the link to the Map/Optimize/Execute/Post-Process workflow, and 'Pagpoproseso Pagkatapos' is a stiff calque.

editor_note: The two rewritten entries are faithful and natural: entry 5 ("maglaan ng saglit… pagsagot sa sumusunod na maikling survey") and entry 12's Credly notice, which keeps every clause and hedge, including "Maaaring ibahagi ng IBM… sa buong mundo" and "Pamamahalaan ito nang naaayon sa mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM".

Entry 21 "Batay sa Gradient" is fine. Entry 17 "Optimisasyon sa Bootstrapping" reverses the relationship: it reads as "optimization within bootstrapping", but the English means bootstrapping the optimization. It is also the only place that uses the Tagalized "Optimisasyon"; everywhere else the page keeps "optimization" ("optimization loop", "naunang optimization"). Entry 25 "Walang Gradient" can read as "the function has no gradient" instead of "an optimizer that doesn't use gradients", and it doesn't match "Gradient-Free" in the parent heading [20] or "gradient-free optimizer" in [26]. Neither slip would mislead a learner, because the body text right below each heading makes the meaning clear.

examples.source: Bootstrapping Optimization
examples.translation: Optimisasyon sa Bootstrapping
examples.suggested: Pag-bootstrap ng Optimization
examples.why: The word order makes bootstrapping the setting for the optimization, when it should be the action done to it. 'Optimisasyon' also clashes with the English 'optimization' used everywhere else in the file, e.g. [5] 'Mag-bootstrap ng optimization loop'.

examples.source: Gradient-Free
examples.translation: Walang Gradient
examples.suggested: Gradient-Free
examples.why: 'Walang Gradient' ('there is no gradient') can suggest the cost function has no gradient, when the point is that the method doesn't use one. It also breaks consistency with [20] 'Gradient-Free na Optimizer' and [26] 'gradient-free optimization algorithm'. If a Tagalog phrase is preferred, 'Hindi Gumagamit ng Gradient' works.

editor_note: Neither rewritten heading would mislead a learner, but both break conventions the rest of the page keeps. Entry 25 renders "Variational theorem" as "Variational na teorema". The paragraph right below it (entry 26), the later heading in entry 45 and entry 48 all keep "variational theorem", so the section heading and its body now name the concept differently. Entry 9 uses "daloy ng trabaho" for "workflow", while entry 5 keeps "workflow", so the same term appears two ways on the page.

examples.source: Variational theorem {#variational-theorem}
examples.translation: Variational na teorema {#variational-theorem}
examples.suggested: Variational theorem {#variational-theorem}
examples.why: Entries 26, 45 and 48 all use 'variational theorem'. Only this heading uses 'teorema', so a reader sees two names for the same concept in one section.

examples.source: Simplified hybrid workflow {#simplified-hybrid-workflow}
examples.translation: Pinasimpleng hybrid na daloy ng trabaho {#simplified-hybrid-workflow}
examples.suggested: Pinasimpleng hybrid na workflow {#simplified-hybrid-workflow}
examples.why: Entry 5 keeps 'workflow' ('workflow ng disenyo ng variational algorithm'). This heading uses 'daloy ng trabaho' for the same term, which is understandable but inconsistent within the file.

editor_note: Entry 19 is wrong. Its link text is a copy of entry 16's title ("Sample-based quantum diagonalization of a chemistry Hamiltonian"), not a translation of the entry's own English. It turns a nuclear Hamiltonian into a chemistry one and drops "Pooled", so the list shows two tutorials with the same title and misdescribes the nuclear-sqd-pooled tutorial. The other six rewritten entries are accurate and read naturally: 18 "para sa pagtatantya ng ground state", 45 "Magpatakbo ng mga quantum workload gamit ang QRMI", 68 "Hanapin ang…", 69/70 "Lutasin ang…" and 88 "gamit ang logical noise models".

examples.suggested: [Pooled sample-based quantum diagonalization ng isang nuclear Hamiltonian](/tutorials/nuclear-sqd-pooled)
